facts.statement: The species was first described by Andrews in 1897.
The species was originally named Tribonyx roberti.
The genus Hovacrex was established by Brodkorb in 1965.
The animal lived during the Late Pleistocene.
Fossils date from 0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Late Pleistocene (0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was a large gallinule found only in Madagascar.
facts.quote: It was a large gallinule that was endemic to Madagascar.

facts.statement: The bird was about the size of the Tasmanian nativehen.
facts.quote: About the size of the Tasmanian nativehen

facts.statement: The absence of wing bones in fossils from Sirabé in central Madagascar makes it uncertain if the species was flightless.
facts.quote: The lack of wing bones in the subfossil material found at Sirabé in central Madagascar makes it uncertain as to whether the species was flightless.

facts.statement: It belongs to the rail family and was originally classified in the genus Tribonyx.
facts.quote: It was a large gallinule that was endemic to Madagascar. About the size of the Tasmanian nativehen, it was originally placed in the same genus, Tribonyx.

facts.statement: It may be synonymous with the genus Gallinula.
facts.quote: Hovacrex may also be synonymous with Gallinula.

facts.statement: Its parent group is the family Rallidae.

rejected.statement: It is classified in the class Aves.
